srikanth-lingala__zip4j_CVE-2018-1002202.releases_exposed: the 1.x line was NEVER fixed (last release 1.3.3, 2019-05-17); on the 2.x line, every release up to v2.3.0
srikanth-lingala__zip4j_CVE-2018-1002202.corroboration: explicit — '#133 Fix for zip slip when file name is similar to directory extracted to'; third-party issue #133 opened 2020-01-21. No CVE was assigned to it.
srikanth-lingala__zip4j_CVE-2018-1002202.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION — phrase this row carefully. ff3d3b34 fixes net.lingala.zip4j.tasks.AbstractExtractFileTask in the 2.x rewrite, NOT the net.lingala.zip4j.unzip.Unzip class our PoV executes. The 1.x line was never fixed; its last release is 1.3.3. Correct wording: 'upstream later closed the same logical sink in the successor codebase', not 'the same code path'. This is also why the executed control errors: the 1.x API the PoV drives does not exist at ff3d3b34. PROVENANCE, now fully explained: the recorded official-fix SHA 59aeea59 does not exist upstream (gh api -> 422; upstream history starts 2019-05-04 and contains ZERO commits touching Unzip.java). It exists in iris-sast/zip4j, which is NOT a mirror or fork (fork=false, parent=null, created 2025-06-30) but a synthetic benchmark repo built from decompiled sources JARs — 59aeea59 is a 2025-07-09 commit titled 'Add decompiled source for 1.3.3 (fixed) from zip4j-1.3.3-sources.jar', child of the 1.3.2 'vulnerable' commit. So our official_fix.patch content is genuine 1.3.3 code; only the SHA is synthetic, and the dataset's github_url for this row points at that reconstructed repo. RE-INTRODUCTION CLAIM CORRECTED: we credited c158768 (2019-09-05, '#55 ZipSlip fix') with re-introducing the boundary-less check in 2.x. Refuted — c158768 only canonicalized the LEFT operand. The real re-introduction is 4c50a6a5 (2019-05-18, 'Outputstreams refractor'), which added the 1.3.3-shaped guard verbatim ONE DAY after 1.3.3 shipped. That makes the recurrence thesis stronger, not weaker: the same defect was written into the rewrite the day after it was fixed in the old line.
srikanth-lingala__zip4j_CVE-2018-1002202.verified_by: human 2026-08-21 + independent agent audit (primary CONFIRMED; re-introduction attribution REFUTED and replaced; provenance of the synthetic SHA established)

nahsra__antisamy_CVE-2022-28367_1.6.5::r.corroboration: explicit — commit message: 'Fix child node removal on style tag processing'
nahsra__antisamy_CVE-2022-28367_1.6.5::r.notes: TWICE-CORRECTED. (1) The first pass said the residual fix first shipped in v1.7.0, i.e. 3 releases exposed; reading the source at each tag shows v1.6.7 already has the reversed loop, so it is 2. (2) The SHA also needed fixing: the change dual-landed. 32e27350 (2022-04-09) is on the 1.6.x lineage and IS an ancestor of v1.6.7 (compare: 2 ahead, 0 behind); 21c4061da0fc (identical subject and author date) is the main-line twin and is NOT in v1.6.7 (compare: diverged) — it is first tagged v1.7.0. Cite 32e27350 for the release claim and 21c4061 for the main-line commit. ROOT CAUSE of the original error: 'git tag --contains 21c4061' answers v1.7.0, because --contains cannot see a cherry-pick onto a release branch. Content-at-tag is the only reliable oracle for 'which release shipped the fix'. NOTE this row is a live-NodeList removal bug, NOT the containment-boundary family. EXECUTED: both PoVs reproduce on unpatched and after the official fix, and are BLOCKED at 21c4061 (exit 1) — falsifiability control passed, independently on two machines.
nahsra__antisamy_CVE-2022-28367_1.6.5::r.verified_by: human 2026-08-21 (per-tag source read) + independent agent audit (confirmed, corrected the SHA) + executed control

yamcs__yamcs_CVE-2023-45277_5.8.6::put_s.releases_exposed: 5.8.8 .. 5.9.8 on the mainline — PLUS yamcs-5.9.8.1 (2025-03-13), a patch-branch release that still ships the boundary-less guard 7 months after 5.10.0 closed it
yamcs__yamcs_CVE-2023-45277_5.8.6::put_s.corroboration: incidental — 4d41784a is Allow symlinks in fs buckets #919; its companion test adds only a symlink test, no sibling-prefix test, so upstream did not know it was closing a traversal gap
yamcs__yamcs_CVE-2023-45277_5.8.6::put_s.notes: CORRECTED after an independent audit REFUTED one of our sub-claims. We said the 5.9.x maintenance line still shipped the gap at yamcs-5.9.12 (2024-12-10), four months after 5.10.0. That is FALSE: 5.9.x received a cherry-pick (fec34d5e, same title/author-date, compare fec34d5e...yamcs-5.9.9 = 46 ahead / 0 behind), so 5.9.9 onward are safe and the last vulnerable mainline 5.9.x is 5.9.8 (2024-07-09), BEFORE 5.10.0. The error came from inferring the guard from a tag date instead of reading the file at that tag. What survives is stronger: yamcs-5.9.8.1 (2025-03-13), a patch branch off 5.9.8, still contains getCanonicalPath().startsWith 7 months after the fix shipped. Guard semantics were also verified empirically on JDK 21: with root .../bkt and sibling .../bkt_evil, objectName ../bkt_evil/victim.txt is ALLOWED by the old guard and REJECTED by the new one, while ../../etc/passwd is rejected by both — i.e. 4d41784a closes exactly the shape these 8 PoVs use. Lag 9.8 months by author date (10.0 by merge-to-master, 9.3 release-to-release; say which).
yamcs__yamcs_CVE-2023-45277_5.8.6::put_s.verified_by: human 2026-08-21 (tag scan) + independent agent audit (confirmed the fix, REFUTED the 5.9.x sub-claim) + re-verified by hand at 5 tags

Adding '&& line_ptr < line_end' caps the iteration count, and the outer loop then exits. No opcode_base == 0 rejection exists at master and none is needed.
